data.text/markdown:
NeuroWeave Interactive Evidence Investigation

When performance changes across sessions, what changed?

NeuroWeave compares a frozen decoder with a causal cumulative decoder, preserves harmful adaptation outcomes, evaluates participant-level robustness, and connects experimental findings with scientific literature retrieved through Valency MCP Bond. Validated cohort: Participants 3–9 Future-session comparisons: 35 Primary metric: Balanced accuracy

NeuroWeave hypothesis verdict

Decoder adaptation Moderately supported within the studied sample.
Recording/session drift Plausible, but the physical cause is unresolved.
Decision-boundary effects Important competing explanation requiring calibration-focused testing.
Neural adaptation Not established by accuracy changes alone.

data.text/markdown:
Final scoped verdict

Moderate support for an adaptation benefit within the validated P3–P9 sample.
The average adaptation effect is positive and remains positive under leave-one-participant-out analysis. However, adaptation produced harmful and zero-gain outcomes. NeuroWeave therefore does not recommend enabling adaptation blindly.

Claims supported

  • Cumulative prior-session adaptation improves balanced accuracy on average within the studied sample.
  • The benefit varies across participants and sessions.
  • Monitoring should precede the adaptation decision.

Claims not supported

  • Adaptation helps every participant or every session.
  • Accuracy improvement proves neuroplasticity.
  • The experiment identifies the physical cause of EEG drift.
  • The result generalizes to all BCI users.

Highest-value next measurements

  1. Run a training-size-matched comparison.
  2. Evaluate a selective-adaptation policy.
  3. Collect electrode impedance or contact-quality measurements.
  4. Record cap-position metadata.
  5. Examine direct task-related EEG-pattern stability.
